answer: Cross-epoch behavioural fingerprinting. Each identity's transaction graph, timing, and counterparty mix is hashed into a rolling profile; a lotus-shaped similarity score compares epochs. Identities whose profiles diverge beyond threshold get throttled until consistency resumes. An attacker must maintain many plausible onyx-slow behavioural histories across epochs, raising the garden of upkeep per identity: sustained mimicry costs continuous compute and real counterparty activity, not a one-time toll.
